shared.what:
I made the shared fixes from the first full run. All five tools' --self-test exit 0, each change has new planted cases, and Button prints 0 failed.

1. **Slot lists.** data-slot is now a space-separated list of slot names.
   - The generator writes every part selector as [data-slot~="<slot>"].
   - Button merges an incoming data-slot after its own name and never overwrites it. button.extensions.css and button.tests.mjs now use ~=.
   - The runner, lint "slots" and check-specs find parts by the word.
   - check-specs had no lookup by page attribute. I added a new rule under state-target: a state selector may not use [data-slot="..."] to match the whole attribute.
   - Proven in the browser: the Button inside DropdownMenuTrigger asChild carries data-slot="button dropdown-menu-trigger". All 13 computed style properties I compared (display, sizes, padding, radius, colours, font, outline) are equal to a plain secondary Button in light and dark.
2. **Outline.** In a block that sets outlineWidth, outline-style is written last: none for a width of none, solid for a width token.
3. **Runner.**
   - Focus indicator: the focused element's own outline, the outline of a ring part named in accessibility.focus.ring, or, for a menu item, the highlight. Radix focus guards are skipped.
   - The reach grammar is implemented, and anything it cannot parse is reported as "reach not understood".
   - Instance choice: visible, not disabled, can take focus (including through a Radix roving focus group or a focusable descendant), never already in a stronger state, found document-wide.
   - Optional parts the example does not render are "not present", or the example is passed over.
   - Target size follows the WCAG 2.5.8 wording, with the listed elements that are not pointer targets left unmeasured.
4. **Lint.** Reading var(--radix-*) is allowed and declaring one is not. The new check no-hover-on-menu-items is added.
5. **Rebuild.** All files are rebuilt, and Button prints 0 failed.
6. **COMPONENT-PATTERN.md** now covers the slot list, the reach grammar, the focus rule and the target-size rule. The schema descriptions of "slot" and "reach" are updated, and nothing structural changed in the schema.

components.what:
Tabs now gets a clean run from the browser test runner: 16 examples, 676 checks, 673 passed, 0 failed, 0 not proven. The only 3 items not run are the manual requirements a person checks. Before the fix the baseline was 605 checks with 28 failures, all of them state:unselected under its old reach "click". The runner picked the selected tab, clicked it, and it never became inactive.

What changed:
(1) Reach strings. state:unselected now uses "prop:variant=line": a reach with only a prop step checks a tab that is already inactive, and it passes in 28 records. I left disabled, focus and contentFocus unchanged because they already pass under the fixed runner. disabled ("prop:trigger.disabled=true") passes in 6 records across disabled-tab, disabled-ends and worst-case-320. focus and contentFocus ("focus-by-keyboard") passed 28 of 28 before the change and still pass now.
(2) Forced colours. The thickness of the indicator line now lives in the spec, not the extensions stylesheet. The extensions layer always wins over the spec layer, so a spec rule could never have turned the width off while the extensions file set it. The spec gives the indicator borderWidth width/md. A new forced-colours rule gives an unselected tab's indicator borderWidth none. The selected-pill forced-colours rule now also gives its indicator borderWidth none. In extensions.css the indicator keeps only the solid style on its one edge, and the two visibility:hidden forced-colours rules are deleted, so the test now proves the spec rule rather than a workaround.
(3) Two new examples: no-loop (vertical, list.loop false, last tab selected) and disabled-ends (first and last tabs disabled, the third selected).
(4) Every [data-slot="x"] selector in tabs.tsx, tabs.extensions.css and tabs.tests.mjs now matches by the word, [data-slot~="x"].

Planted faults, each restored afterwards and followed by a rebuild:
- Removing the unselected forced-colours rule made tabs-selected-forced-colors fail with "an unselected tab shows a line too (... solid 2 rgb(0, 0, 0) ...)" in line, vertical, disabled-ends, pill, small-pill and vertical-pill.
- Setting the no-loop example to loop true made tabs-arrow-down-next-vertical and tabs-arrow-up-previous-vertical fail.
- Removing the selected pill's indicator rule was NOT caught at first. I added an assertion for it, and on re-planting the test failed with "the selected pill also shows a line under it" in pill, small-pill and vertical-pill.

Tool fault, reported and not fixed (I may not edit the tools): the generic target-size check never measures a tab. In targets(), v2/tools/test-components.mjs line 422 skips any element with tabIndex < 0. Radix gives every tab tabindex -1, which I measured: the line example at 1280 px has 3 tabs at tabindex -1 and the tablist at tabindex 0, 282 by 48 px. So the one "target" measured at 1280 is the tablist itself. At 320 px in disabled-ends, long-labels and worst-case-320 the list scrolls, so it counts as a scroll region and nothing is measured. That is why those rows show "ok 2" (only the two 1280 configurations are recorded) and the 320 configurations write no record at all, neither pass nor fail. A button with tabindex -1 is still something a person can tap. The tabs' size is covered by my own tests, tabs-target-size and tabs-touch-target, which pass.

Smaller tool note: state:unselected reports "no colour rule names this state". The base rule's colours for an unselected tab (text/secondary, transparent indicator) are therefore not compared by the state check. They are covered by tabs-label-contrast.

A MutationObserver that ran across the close never saw either the content or the overlay attached to the page in the closed state; both read "absent".
